output.methodChoice: D (competing hypotheses) with unstructured reasoning: five rival explanations, and a few discriminating records could rule them in or out.
output.brief:
The evidence points to bad data, not operators or printers. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol, valid only from 1 March 2027. The old 24-month value is still the one in effect. Yet from 4 Oct the line integration service sent 36 months to the printers. Every job since then has an expiry 12 months too late. All 47 Veltranol jobs show no operator overrides. The printer printed exactly what it received. The camera passed every carton because it only checks print against the job. Jobs before 4 Oct were correct, including those after the firmware change and those set up by agency operators. Two jobs on Line 1 day shift, run by permanent staff, were also wrong. Why the future-dated value was used is not yet established. That is the vendor's claim versus the evidence.

Do not discipline or remove the agency operators. Do not switch off camera checks. Reset the Veltranol record, extend the hold to every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse, and add a second-person check at setup. Check other products with October edits, especially the two with later valid-from dates. Ask the vendor to explain the behaviour. I'm fairly sure of the Veltranol cause. Other products are unchecked.
